behavior: An invoice can carry a supply date (when the work was done or delivered), shown on the form, the invoice page and the PDFs (PLAN 10.2)
acceptance: The create request takes an optional supplyDate (YYYY-MM-DD, the day the work was done or delivered); a bad date is 422 invalid_value. It is part of the idempotency hash (requests without it hash as before), never changes like the other details, and comes back as supplyDate (null when not set) on the owner's and the public reads.
The invoice PDF, the canceled invoice PDF and the receipt show Supply date beside Issued when it is set, and nothing when it is not.
New invoice has an optional Supply date picker in the Dates panel (not on Request money) and the owner's invoice page shows it in Details; axe 0 and no sideways scroll at 390 px.

Checked and OK: migration 00031 trigger = 00029 (latest) + supply_date in both tuples; view keeps all 00029 columns + supply_date; Down restores 00029 view and trigger exactly, then drops the column (diffed). Hash: without supplyDate the bytes are unchanged; '|supplyDate=' cannot be confused with returnUrl, country/taxId or lines, which all start with '|"'. Validation: 422 for 2026-02-30 and 31.10.2026, year 0 refused. Every read goes through invoices_current (create, replay, owner GET, public GET, list, cancel); options get empty Details, so supply_date is NULL on option rows; null when unset. PDFs: I rendered one with 4 facts and it fits (width/4). Web: zod nullable, DatePicker in Dates hidden on Request money, sent as supplyDate, a 422 maps to the field, Details row after Created; e2e and axe pass. Readers that do not show it, all acceptable for this acceptance: pay page (the payer gets it on the PDF), invoice list, form preview (mirrors the pay page), emails (they show no due date either), new-from-closed (copies no dates). Minor notes: formatDueDate now formats a supply date (a name like formatDay would fit); the two adjacent '{request ? null : ...}' blocks could be one; name="supplyDate"/text("supplyDate") repeat INVOICE_FIELDS.supplyDate the same way the dueDate code does.
